fields.description:
# compact-on-close holds the store write lock for MINUTES, starving concurrent writers — and "isolated" worktrees share one store

## The two facts together are the defect

### 1. The worktrees are NOT isolated — they symlink to ONE store

`/Users/joeoakhart/agent-5200-diag/.tickets-tracker` is a **symlink** to
`/Users/joeoakhart/rebar/.tickets-tracker`. So is `/Users/joeoakhart/probe-status-e34a/.tickets-tracker`.
All three resolve to the same path and to the **same lock inode (420945058)**.
`lock.canonical_tracker` (`_store/lock.py:124-127`) realpaths deliberately so that they contend on one
lock — which is correct behaviour for correctness, and means every parallel agent session serialises
through a single write lock even though each believes it has its own worktree.

Two live `rebar transition ... closed` processes were running against this store during the incident
(from `agent-5200-diag` and `probe-status-e34a`).

### 2. compact-on-close holds that lock across an entire reduce + retire + git commit

`_commands/compact.py:178` takes the same write lock and holds it across the whole critical section
(`compact.py:186` onward), and it is invoked right after every close at
`_commands/transition_close.py:92-104`.

Measured from the tracker's own git log: a **2m17s gap** with nothing landing between
`2a8f02ce14 SIGNATURE e39f` (12:28:38) and `b2e28d2273 COMPACT e39f` (12:30:55). The next commit is
d582's STATUS at 12:30:56 — one second after the compaction released.

### The consequence

A concurrent writer's 60s lock budget (`lock.py:73-74`: 30s x 2 attempts) is consumed entirely inside
one compaction window. That is what dropped a durable record in
[rebar:ab54-f19f-d5bd-422c] — the close's PASS `COMPLETION_VERDICT` sidecar got its single 60s shot
during the gap and lost it.

`flock` is also not FIFO, so a waiter can additionally be starved by a stream of short writers rather
than by one long holder.

Corroborating symptom: `2bc7-d77b-641c-42aa` carries **two** PASS sidecars (12:34:22 and 12:36:31) —
a close that had to be retried under the same contention.

### Diagnosability gap found along the way

**The lock records no holder identity that survives contention.** The fcntl leg (`lock.py:552`) records
no pid at all, and the only owner stamp lives in `.ticket-write.lock.d/owner` (`lock.py:36`), which is
removed on release — so a timed-out waiter cannot say who blocked it. The holder above was identified by
inferring from the commit timeline, not from any recorded pid. A `LockTimeout` that cannot name the
holder is expensive to diagnose under fleet load.

Also observed, separately: `llm/enrich_drain.py:243-251`'s "cheap gate" logs
`enrich drain gate check took 300-800ms (> 20 ms budget)` on nearly every command against this
3174-ticket store, and `overlap_drain=async` detaches drain CHILD processes that write events
(`enrich_drain.py:254-256`), making them additional lock contenders. None committed inside the measured
gap, so they are not the holder here.

### Residue

An untracked `.tickets-tracker/.tmp-event-lpusw0uh` (mtime 10:42) predates this incident and belongs to
some other failed or killed write. `event_append.py:470-472` does unlink the staging temp on
`LockTimeout`, so this is from a different failure mode — worth sweeping and worth knowing that
something leaves temps behind.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] **Compaction's lock hold time is reduced from 48.1s to ~1.0s** (REMEDIATED wording — the
      original criterion said the lock is "no longer held across the whole reduce + git-commit
      section", which describes R2, a fix that was CONSIDERED AND DECLINED). What landed instead is
      R1: `resolve_event_commit`'s per-event `git log --full-history` became ONE directory-scoped
      walk. Measured on the real 71,041-commit store: 4-file ticket 29.81s->1.05s (28x), 25 files
      193.16s->4.72s (41x), 73 files 546.00s->4.27s (128x), 155 files 1165.54s->2.09s (557x), zero
      mismatches across 257 events. The structural point is that the after-column NO LONGER GROWS
      with event count — cost is per-compaction, not per-event, so the previously UNBOUNDED growth
      is gone. The ledger deliberately STAYS INSIDE the lock: at ~1s there is no reason to accept
      R2's race, where a stale ledger could omit a folded signed event and break `verify-authorship`.
- [x] **A `LockTimeout` names the holder** (REMEDIATED — the original said "pid + worktree"; the
      operator scoped R5 to EXISTING machinery, and the v2 ownership stamp records host/ns/pid/start,
      not worktree). Delivered: `flock: could not acquire lock after 60s (holder: host=... pid=...
      start=... held=...s pid_state=live)`. `pid_state` follows the same refuse-without-proof rule
      reclamation uses, so the message can never imply a reclaim the lock itself would decline.
      Degraded cases are explicit and tested: no stamp / unrecognised stamp / incomplete stamp.
- [x] **Compact-on-close stands aside when the lock is busy** (R3, added after the operator
      established the load is INTERMITTENT rather than sustained, which removed the indefinite-
      deferral objection). `write_lock_is_busy()` probes both legs in `acquire`'s order at zero
      deadline, releases fcntl in a `finally`, removes a successful mkdir probe immediately, and
      FAILS OPEN so a probe failure degrades to today's behaviour. Skipping proven a correctness
      no-op end-to-end: close succeeds, event log byte-identical, next uncontended compaction folds
      to the same reduced state.
- [x] **The root cause is documented with measurements** so it cannot be rediscovered from scratch:
      the shared-store-by-symlink topology (`lock.canonical_tracker`, `_store/lock.py:124-127`) is
      CORRECT and is what makes compaction safe; the defect was hold DURATION, of which 99.2% was
      read-only git archaeology inside the mutation.

## Not done — deliberately, and where each lives

- **Write loss on lock-acquire timeout.** The original criterion "concurrent close from two
  worktrees does not drop a durable record" is NOT met. Measured: one long holder + six concurrent
  `rebar comment`s = 6/6 failures at 60s with ALL SIX WRITES PERMANENTLY LOST. R1/R3/R5 reduce the
  CAUSE of contention but do not change the failure shape when a writer still loses the race.
  Owned by **`10c3-5a33-2e25-4584`**, which also carries the un-run post-R1 re-measurement — at ~1s
  holds the timeout may now be unreachable in practice, and that measurement should come first.
- **R2 / R4** (hoisting work out of the lock) — declined; R1 makes them unnecessary and they carry
  real atomicity exposure.
- **R6** (spool-and-adopt) — declined here as a product decision; folded into `10c3`.
- **Per-ticket locking** — recorded as a FUTURE consideration for a second round if this one
  underdelivers. Analysis preserved in this ticket's comments: the logical mutation IS per-ticket
  and HLC is not a blocker (own short lock, disposable state), but `git add`/`git commit` are
  repo-global so the commit step serialises regardless.
- **Two minor items from the original criteria are UNOWNED**: documenting the shared-store topology
  where agents are told to use a fresh worktree, and sweeping the stray `.tmp-event-*` residue plus
  identifying its source failure mode. Neither is covered by `10c3`. They are recorded here rather
  than silently dropped; file them if they matter.
